_mechanisms_active: Everything in B (Method 1, face_says_stranger gate, face_veto)
ByteTrack ID-switch guard — a cached code contradicted by a gate-passing face for id_switch_contradiction_limit (default 2) consecutive cycles is dropped, forcing re-identification
_mechanisms_disabled: evidence gating — a sighting/photo is still logged the MOMENT a code is current (cached or freshly matched), even before the guard above has had the 2 cycles it needs to notice a contradiction. The guard corrects the code eventually; it does not retroactively un-log evidence filed during the 1-2 cycles before it fires.
_registration_note: Unaffected by these two flags: minting still always requires a visible face, in every config.
_expected_risk: Fixes cross-video/cross-occlusion ID theft that B is exposed to, but there is a real window — up to id_switch_contradiction_limit analysis cycles — where a hijacked track can still write 1-2 sighting rows / photos under the wrong code before the guard catches it. D closes that window by refusing to log evidence until a fresh face directly confirms the code.
